messages:
amanda: Quick sync — I'm about to land the change that flips the default model for /v2/generate to 'redwood-large:v2'. Before I push, quick Qs on compatibility and rollout strategy.

amanda: main concerns: 1) clients that rely on previous default output shape, 2) pin header behaviour, 3) deprecation notice window.

josh: thanks for the heads up. do we have a semantic guarantee that v2 won't change the response envelope?

amanda: short answer: we tried to keep the envelope stable but there is a small opt-in field 'meta.source_version' added for telemetry. not breaking.

lee: the bigger risk is model output delta — responses will differ and some downstream evals might regress. we should gate with canary and a gradual rollout.

priya: for pinning: client can set `X-Model-Accept: redwood-large:v1` or `X-Model-Pin: redwood-large:v1`. which header are we standardizing on?

amanda: current plan: accept header is advisory; pin header is the explicit contract. if pin present we must never route to a different version. fallback policy only for unpinned requests.

josh: can we add an explicit 400 when a pinned model is unavailable vs silently routing to fallback? i worry about silent behavior breaking strict clients.

lee: +1 for explicit failure when pinned unavailable. ops can provide a well-documented retry/backoff pattern.

ops-bot: NOTE: rolling out pinned-fail-fast behaviour will require a schema bump in the client SDK docs and a short migration note.

amanda: decision: pinned requests -> fail-fast with 422 + error.reason = "pinned_model_unavailable". non-pinned -> routed according to policy + header negotiation. agreed?

priya: agreed. pls add a flag to the rollout so enterprise accounts can opt-out for 2 weeks while they update clients.

amanda: adding enterprise opt-out param to the rollout config. also planning canary at 5% global traffic for 24h then 25% for 48h, metrics to watch: latency P95, generation token cost, prompt-level quality for top 10 prompts.

josh: CR ping @lee @priya — I left a small shim in the router: `if (req.headers['x-model-pin']) { ensurePinnedAvailableOrThrow(); }` — needs a unit test and an integration test with simulated capacity loss.

lee: I'll take the unit tests. @priya can you do the integration harness in staging? note: we need to simulate a model eviction scenario.

priya: yep, will add a fault injection case to the model manager test suite.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/flip-default-model -> staging (build 4821). runbook: rollback with `--default-model redwood-large:v1` flag.

amanda: timelines: push to staging today, smoke tests + CRs by EOD, canary roll tomorrow if green. everyone ok with that cadence?

josh: sounds good. i'll monitor regressions and have rollback ready. :thumbsup:

lee: sending a short comms draft for deprecation window: "Default model for /v2/generate will change on 2026-04-12. Clients that rely on exact output should pin the model header. We recommend testing with the canary via `?rollout=canary`." will drop in #announcements for review.

amanda: please include migration snippets for SDKs (node/py) — show how to pin and how to opt into canary. low-friction examples.

priya: action items: 1) lee: comms draft (PR) 2) josh: add unit + integration tests 3) amanda: rollout config + enterprise opt-out 4) me: fault injection harness. deadline: EOD today.

amanda: thanks — tagging this thread resolved when PRs merged. ping me on the CR if anyone needs pairing.

josh: ack.

lee: ack.

priya: ack.
